title: Prophets themselves were tossed with doubts about God’s favor, as the Psalms show
source_text: XIX. Patet id exemplis Prophetarum ipsorum quae leguntur in sacra Scriptura. Qualem enim animi aestum experiebatur in se sanctus Propheta, & quibus jactabatur dubitationibus, circa Dei gratiam, favorem atque auxilium, dum sic queritur Psal. 77. Num in aeternum projiciet Deus? & non apponet ut complacitior sit adhuc? Aut in finem misericordiam suam abscindet, a generatione in generationem? Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus? Aut continebit in ira sua misericordias suas? Et Psal. 88. Domine Deus salutis meae, in die clamavi, & nocte coram te. ... Quare Domine repellis orationem meam: avertis faciem tuam a me? ... Transierunt irae tuae: & terrores tui conturbaverunt me. Circundederunt me sicut aqua: tota die circundederunt me simul.
pass_a_gloss: This is plain from the examples of the Prophets themselves which are read in holy Scripture. For what agitation of mind the holy Prophet experienced in himself, and with what doubts he was tossed concerning God’s grace, favor, and help, when he thus complains in Psalm 77: Will God cast off forever? and will he be favorable no more? Has he cut off his mercy forever? Has God forgotten to be merciful? Has he in anger shut up his mercies? And in Psalm 88: O Lord God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you… Why, Lord, do you cast off my prayer and turn your face from me?… Your wraths have gone over me; and your terrors have troubled me. They surrounded me like water; all day they surrounded me together.
pass_b_english: The Psalms record prophets tossed by doubts about God’s abiding mercy.
Psalms 77 and 88 voice fear that God has cast off and shut up his compassions.
